## Summary

The mcp entrypoint added by `kilted-nuclear-bronco` clones the `tickets` branch SYNCHRONOUSLY
before `exec "$@"`. That branch has **199,846 commits**. The blue-green readiness gate allows
**120 seconds** (`autodeploy.sh:130` `MCP_HEALTH_TIMEOUT=120`). The clone cannot finish in time,
so the server never starts listening, `/health` never answers, and autodeploy removes the new
container and rolls back — on every deploy.

**`main` currently cannot deploy the mcp service at all.** This is a regression from my own
merged change, not a pre-existing fault.

## Evidence (from the box, 2026-08-26)

    AUTODEPLOY_ERROR {"reason": "mcp-unhealthy", "detail": "new mcp container
      rebar-mcp-11f6e61c732b-8093 failed /health within 120s; removing it, leaving the OLD
      upstream live"}
    AUTODEPLOY_ERROR {"reason": "deploy_failed", "detail": "target=11f6e61c732b... fail#1 backoff=60s"}

`11f6e61c732b` is exactly "feat(mcp): provision the mcp ticket store" (Gerrit 2231).

    deployed-sha:    078ca376cee3...            (predates the merge)
    running:         rebar-mcp-078ca376cee3-8092  Up 43 minutes (healthy)
    nginx upstream:  server 127.0.0.1:8092;       (correct — pointing at the OLD container)
    tickets branch:  199,846 commits

The nginx upstream is CORRECT and the old container is healthy, so the rollback works exactly as
designed. The endpoint is serving stale code because the new code cannot boot.

## Root cause of the design error

I modelled the entrypoint on the review-bot's (`Dockerfile.reviewbot:143-166`), which also
clones at entrypoint. But the review-bot has NO blue-green readiness deadline — it is a
stop-and-start service. The mcp service is promoted only after answering `/health` within a hard
120s window. Copying a blocking-clone pattern into a service with a readiness gate is what broke
it. The soft-failure posture I designed ("no PAT ⇒ clone deferred, container still boots") only
covers the ABSENT-credential case; with the credential PRESENT the clone runs and blocks.

## Fix

Do not block startup on the clone. Start the server first and converge the store in the
background, so the container becomes healthy immediately and the store appears when it is ready.

This composes correctly with the read guard already on main: while the clone is still running,
tracker reads raise `store_uninitialized` — an honest, machine-readable "not ready yet" — rather
than returning `[]` and pretending the tracker is empty. That is exactly the degradation the
read guard was built to provide.

Also worth bounding the clone cost itself (199k commits is expensive to re-clone on every fresh
container), but correctness first: unblock the boot.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The mcp container answers `/health` well within `MCP_HEALTH_TIMEOUT` regardless of whether
      a tickets clone is in progress, so blue-green promotion succeeds.
- [x] The store still converges: once the clone completes, tracker reads return real tickets.
      Verified LIVE on the box: 2763 tickets readable through https://.../mcp after convergence.
- [ ] NOT MET — split out, not silently ticked. While the clone is in flight, tracker reads
      still return `[]`, not `store_uninitialized`. `_reads._tracker` keys on
      `os.path.isdir`, and the clone target directory EXISTS while it is being populated, so
      the guard does not fire. The absent-store case IS covered (that guard shipped); the
      present-but-unusable case is not, and cannot be fixed here — it needs the read guard to
      treat a directory that is not a usable store as uninitialized, which changes core read
      semantics repo-wide and must preserve the contract that an empty INITIALIZED store still
      reads `[]`. Tracked as `beton-inversive-stag`; see also `fathomable-yester-thrip`, where
      the same residual is recorded.
- [x] A clone failure still leaves the container serving (soft posture preserved).
      `mcp-entrypoint.sh:140` reports the failure and provisioning returns; `exec "$@"` still runs.
- [x] Regression coverage asserts the entrypoint does not block `exec` on the clone.
      Proof: `test_mcp_entrypoint_does_not_block_boot_on_the_tickets_clone` (on main).

## Verification

    .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py -q -p no:randomly
    bash -n on the generated entrypoint

The test has teeth when: restoring the synchronous clone makes the new assertion FAIL.
